post_topic: Why the audit was wrong — and what actually fixed it
image_description:
Single standalone diagram. One concept only. No panels, no grids, no collages. Full bleed 1080x1080px white background.

Title at top center in bold: "The Audit Was Wrong — Because It Never Touched the System"

Diagram flows left to right in three columns.

Left column labeled "Static Review" in navy. Contains three stacked boxes with rounded corners: box 1 labeled "Config Files", box 2 labeled "Source Code", box 3 labeled "Documentation". Each box has a small document icon. A dashed border surrounds all three boxes with a small amber callout label reading "Assumptions — not findings".

Center column labeled "Verification Gate" in amber. Contains a single prominent box with a bold amber border, labeled "Live System Check". Inside the box, three lines of monospace-style text: "curl [endpoint]", "psql -c 'SELECT ...'", "dig [domain]". An amber callout arrow points to this box from the left column with label "Every claim must pass through here".

Right column labeled "Verified Findings" in blue (#5a96ff). Contains three stacked boxes with solid blue borders: box 1 labeled "Confirmed Response", box 2 labeled "Actual Query Result", box 3 labeled "Real DNS Output". A solid blue arrow connects each right-column box back to the verification gate in the center.

At the bottom center, a single horizontal navy banner with white text reading: "If you can't show the live output, you have a hypothesis — not a finding."

Navy #0A0F1E primary elements, blue #5a96ff highlights, amber #F5A623 callouts and important labels. Clean sans-serif font. Real cloud provider logos where relevant. Small text "Kelvin Davis" bottom right corner. Professional LinkedIn infographic style similar to ByteByteGo. White background. No dark backgrounds.
